The FX slider in the FFB menu can enhance tire forces such as scrub, brake lockup, the feeling of over and understeer as well as the road surface irregularities.
Tires and brakes are at their optimal temperature range while green in the HUD Display - blue is under temp, yellow is over, and red is critically over temp at risk of failure.
The vehicle weight listed in the info above includes 85kg for the driver with complete racing gear, as well as other car fluids not including fuel.
Adjust your brake ducts to best suit the current track conditions - a higher brake duct setting will cool them more, while a lower will retain more heat.
Adjustable onboard anti-roll bars and brake bias are valuable tools to adjust the car balance as the tires wear and fuel tank runs low.
Brake ducts and radiator openings are important to cool brake and engine temperatures, but also add a small amount of aero drag & lift - don´t run them more open than you need to!

When driving on a drying track, try to make sure to keep the loaded outside wheels in a given corner inside the dry line - stepping them on a wet patch may lead to running wide and losing a lot of time!
The Low Force Boost slider in the FFB menu can help enhance low-end forces at the center - weaker wheels should use higher values, while DD wheels should have it low or zeroed.
Setup modifications are auto-saved and marked by "*" once it has modified from factory defaults - defaults may still be restored by clicking the "Reset to Default" button.
Keep an eye on the ambient and track temperatures in the monitor screen - they are critical to keep tire and brake conditions within their optimal range and avoid excessive wear.
The track altitude and resulting atmospheric pressure has a big impact in performance - the higher the location, the more aspirated engines will suffer, and the less aero will work.
Set your brake pressure just high enough to avoid locking up on the hardest braking zone - that may be determined by monitoring the brake disc temperatures.
Make sure to select and / or adjust your pit strategy in the In-Car menu before coming in for a pit stop.
The telemetry HUD page features various widgets that can help you better set up your car and force feedback.
Time Trial Mode allows you to measure up against the fastest drivers in any given car-track combo, and also download the setups used in their fastest times.
In cars with adjustable boost, higher values will generate more engine heat - make sure to adjust radiator opening accordingly to cool it down.
Make sure to respect the white lines exiting the pits in order to not get a penalty or cause collisions with approaching traffic.
If you are using headphones, make sure to select "Headphone Mix" in the Audio settings.
Adjusting field of view (FOV) correctly is crucial for an accurate perception of speed and distances.
If the session forecast is set to real or random weather, the chances of rain will vary according to the climate of the region.
Long tracks may see rain falling harder on some points of the circuit, and less in others - keep that in mind before diving into the pits!

The class of opponents you will be competing against:    - Identical Opponents: AI competitors race in the same vehicle that you have selected.    - Same Class: AI competitors race in the same vehicle class as the vehicle that you have selected.    - Multi-Class: Allows you to configure races with a maximum of 10 vehicle classes. The first slot always matches the vehicle class of the car you have selected in Vehicle Selection, but you can add 9 additional classes for the AI to compete with.

Increases or decrease the level of smoothing and filtering of bumps as the cockpit camera tracks the virtual horizon. Higher values filter more bumps and result in a slower movement towards the horizon when the car pitches/rolls.    With 'Use Legacy Head Movement' mode enabled a setting of 0 fixes cockpit cameras firmly to the car. At higher values the amount of camera movement relative to the car increases.    NOTE: This setting affects camera movement induced by the cars movement only. G-force effects are controlled separately below.
The number of track limit warnings that will be issued to a driver before a drive-through or time penalty is given.

When set to "MAX AVAILABLE" the number of opponents will be automatically set to the maximum supported value without duplicating liveries. For a race of identical vehicles with 10 available liveries the value would be 9.

This controls how aggressive the traction control system is.    Higher values allow less wheel slip before the system will cut throttle to prvent wheelspin. This can be beneficial in low grip situations such as a wet track, or when tyre wear must be managed closely.    Low values allow more slip, and are good for high grip situations: dry track, slick tyres, optimal weather.

This setting allows you to set the starting state of the track surface including if it is wet or already rubbered in.    If set to 'Default Progressing' this session will take the rubber state from the previous session (or the 'Medium' preset if it is the first session of the weekend). Any other setting will apply that preset at the session start regardless of previous session end states.    eg. To start a weekend with light rubber then progress each session based on track running set Practice='Light Rubber', Qualifying='Default Progressing', and Race='Default Progressing'    Wet presets are unavailable when using real weather as the starting state is determined by the real weather prior to the event.

When set to 'Units', suspension settings on the vehicle setup screen will be displayed as a range of steps from the minimum to maximum available setting.    When set to 'Rates' they will be displayed as their actual rates.    In both cases the total range and step between settings are equal.
When enabled a timed race session will end one full lap after the the race duration ends.
This setting determines if refuelling is allowed during pit stops.

When enabled the Limited Tyre Sets option determines the maximum number of new tyre sets players have available for the event as a whole. Each time a tyre set is used on track its last state is maintained and any future use of that tyre will start with the previous wear and compound applied.
the ICM Auto-Close option controls the length of time after the last user input that the In Car Management menu will automatically close

Dertermines whether the In Car Management menu maintains the current menu position or is reset when the menu closes.    None : The current page and menu selection will be maintained.    Default Option: The currently active page will be maintained but the default menu option will be selected.    Default Page: Both the page and menu option will be reset to default.    (Delayed): These options do the same as their non-delayed counterparts but the reset will take place 30 seconds after the menu closes.

The Steering Lock is the maximum number of degrees of rotation of the front wheels.     A lower Steering Lock value increases the amount of steering wheel movement needed per degree of front wheel rotation,  allowing for finer steering control. Increasing the Steering Lock value will give more responsive steering, decreasing the amount of input needed, and making the car more sensitive to steering input.    Care should be taken to ensure there is enough available lock to negotiate the tightest corner on the circuit at racing speed.

Control Assignment:    Click or activate the row of the assignment you wish to edit to start the binding process.    To bind a button, press and release the button when prompted.    To bind an axis such as a pedal or wheel, when prompted, move the axis through at least 50% of its range then return to the zero or centre position.

Sets the mode of the HUD track map.    The 'Static' mode has a fixed map showing the whole track.    The 'Dynamic' mode offers a zoomed map oriented to the players direction of travel.
The volume of wind related sound effects, ranging from 100 (highest) to 0 (lowest).

- Custom offers steering torque around steering axis with no road vibration, damping or friction or allows you to fully configured FFB settings within ffb_custom_settings.txt file located in Documents/Automobilista 2/    - Default adds damping, friction, limited vibrations with a small amount of chassis feedback    - Default+ adds some understeer drop-off, more chassis feedback for feeling the cars weight transfer

Scales the vertical vibration part of signal, vibration produced by tires on heavy slippage, drivetrain vibration / pulses; it also scales chassis effects (lateral acceleration, yaw, weight transfer) present in Default and Default+.

LFB amplifies "light forces“ close to zero/center, gradually rolling off amplification as force output increases. Use for low torque wheels to enhance small signals that may be missed and reduce the lightness around the center. DD wheels should set low or zeroed.

Adds resistance to help prevent oscillations and governs how quickly you can steer from left to right. Lower values allows you to steer quicker with less resistance whilst higher values makes steering slower with more resistance.
Resets all vehicles FFB gain adjusted within the quick setup menu back to 100%.
Scales AI performance in wet conditions relative to the main AI Skill setting; adjust if the AI is too fast or slow compared to its dry performance
Select your active controller preset from up to 5 personal saved controller slots. Presets named (eg. 'User Set 1') are default presets shipped with the game until you modify and save.
This option allows to edit the name of your active controller preset.
This option allows you to copy the settings from another preset into your active controller preset.
This option allows you to enable or disable 'Full Course Yellow' cautions for your race weekend event.
The volume of your engine sounds, ranging from 100 (highest) to 0 (lowest).

When Private Session is set to 'Solo', each driver will compete in isolation with no other vehicles on track as they would in a superpole or oval-style qualifying.     When set to 'Same Class' each class competes in isolation from vehicles of other classes.
Damage Scale determines the amount of damage your vehicle receives when making contact with a opponents vehicle or trackside object.

Random Failures determines whether your vehicle (including Ai) is prone to random failures during a session or not. There are 4 options to choose from:    - Off: By turning off this option, you will prevent random failures from being active during a session.  - x2, x3, x4, x5, x10: These options accelerate random failures by the multiplying number.  - Authentic: By setting this option, random failures will occur at a rate similar to real life.  - Sync To Race: By setting this option, the amount of random failures will occur at a rate that is believable to the race length set.
Enables or disables fading effect when switching between higher and lower detail models at distance on some trackside objects and foliage.
Forces all clients to disable collisions with dynamic trackside objects such as cones, tyres, and brake markers.
Enables/Disables collisions and physics effects on dynamic trackside objects such as cones, bollards, and brake markers. Setting may be overridden by MP server and TT rules.
Enables or disables on-screen confirmation messages for changes to onboard vehicle settings such as TC/ABS level, Brake Bias, ERS modes, etc
Allows drivers to use the vehicle reset control bind to return to the track
Enables the additional ICM page for in-car adjustment of hud options
When enabled the last used setup for the current vehicle will be autoloaded at the start of an event.

Parc Ferme: Once a vehicle leaves the pitlane for the first time in a qualifying session, its setup is locked from further changes with the exception of tyre compound and some limited options to allow balance changes.    Default Setup: Forces the use or default setups and limits changes to tyre compound, fuel levels, and a small selection of changes to aid tuning for different controllers. Changes can be made at any time.

Parallax Occlusion Mapping adds depth and lighting to flat objects without increasing model complexity    Low: Enables Parallax Occlusion Mapping  Medium: Increases the quality and enables hard self-shadowing  High: Further increases the quality and enables soft self-shadowing

The Lap Limit setting defines the maximum number of laps each driver may complete in this session including in/out laps.    With a Stint Limit enabled, the Lap Limit applies to each stint rather than the session as a whole.    Exceeding the Lap Limit at any time will result in disqualification from the session.

The Stint Limit sets the maximum number of times a driver may leave the pits to set laps on track before they are locked to the garage.    New stints can be started by passing through the pit lane or returning to the garage.    Exceeding the Stint Limit at any time will result in disqualification from the session.
